prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right lawyer depends on your case details and priorities (severity of injuries, insurance limits, whether you need a trial lawyer, language needs, budget, etc.). I can help you find a great attorney, but first here’s how to choose one and what to look for.

What to look for
- Relevant experience: lots of recent car-accident/personal-injury cases and outcomes like yours (catastrophic injury, soft-tissue, wrongful death, uninsured motorist, etc.).
- Trial experience: if your case may need to go to trial, choose an attorney who actually tries cases and has courtroom wins.
- Track record: settlements/verdicts, peer recognitions (Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell AV ratings), client reviews.
- Board certification: Texas Board of Legal Specialization offers certification in Personal Injury Trial Law — that’s a meaningful credential.
- Communication and accessibility: clear point of contact, prompt replies.
- Fee structure: contingency fee (common in PI cases) and how costs are handled; get everything in writing.
- Local knowledge: familiarity with Houston courts, judges, local medical providers, and insurers can help.
- Resources: firms that can front costs for medical records, experts, and litigation if needed.

Questions to ask at a free consult
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Who will handle my case day to day (partner or associate)?
- What is your success/settlement history for similar injuries?
- What is your contingency fee and what other costs will I owe?
- How do you handle medical liens and unpaid medical bills?
- Expected timeline and likely value range for my case?
- Can you provide references from former clients?

Where to look and verify
- Texas Board of Legal Specialization (for board certification)
- State Bar of Texas (disciplinary history)
- Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, AVVO, Google/Yelp, Better Business Bureau
- Local groups: Houston Bar Association, Texas Trial Lawyers Association (TTLA)

Practical notes
- Statute of limitations in Texas for most personal-injury claims is 2 years from the crash — don’t delay contacting a lawyer.
- Contingency fees commonly run ~33% for settlements, higher if the case goes to trial or appeal — confirm in writing.
- Most reputable firms offer a free initial consultation and take cases on contingency (no recovery, no fee).

If you want, tell me:
- your ZIP code or neighborhood in Houston
- date of the crash and injuries sustained
- whether fault is disputed and insurance limits (if known)
I can then suggest several well-regarded Houston personal-injury attorneys/firms to contact and help you prioritize who to call first.
